		texture:SetAtlas(atlas.atlas)

items.what: SetStopLook's atlas branch (Looks.lua:119-122) re-implements ns.FitAtlas (Looks.lua:91-100, same file) for a size-by-size box: size/max(w,h) == min(size/w, size/h). Canonical: ns.FitAtlas(texture, art.atlas, size, size).
items.why: Both set the atlas and fit native width/height into the box without stretching (the AGENTS.md never-stretch rule). Only difference: FitAtlas re-queries C_Texture.GetAtlasInfo while Art() cached it; Art already proved the atlas exists, so FitAtlas cannot return false here. A change to the fit rule (e.g. pixel snapping) would land in one copy only.

items.quote:
local atlas = art --[[@as {atlas: string, width: number, height: number}]]
		texture:SetAtlas(atlas.atlas)
		local scale = size / math.max(atlas.width, atlas.height)
items.what: SetStopLook's atlas branch (Looks.lua:119-122) re-implements ns.FitAtlas, defined 20 lines above in the same file (Looks.lua:91-100), for a size-by-size box. Canonical home: ns.FitAtlas; the branch becomes ns.FitAtlas(texture, art.atlas, size, size). Compass.lua SetIcon (Compass.lua:70-76) is a third copy of the same fit.
items.why: size / max(w, h) equals min(size / w, size / h), so both produce the same width and height; the only difference is that Art() caches the atlas dimensions while FitAtlas calls C_Texture.GetAtlasInfo again (a cheap lookup, and Art already proved the atlas exists, so FitAtlas cannot return false here). The fit is the 'never stretch art' rule the project enforces; a fix to it (rounding, a minimum size) would have to land in each copy. tests/looks_spec.lua checks both SetStopLook and FitAtlas sizes and would cover the change.
items.reason: The existing looks_spec.lua passes, but the proposed replacement, tested entirely in memory, fails 'art looked up once per kind'. SetStopLook uses cached dimensions while FitAtlas performs fresh lookups, establishing a tested constraint supporting the lens's performance-specialization exception.

items.quote: if held.source == "you" and incoming.source ~= "you" and now - held.seen < OWN_TRUST then
items.what: Sighting source is the closed set "you"|"player" typed as bare `string` (types/Addon.lua SPFAnchor.source and SPFDeparture.source) and compared by literal at Model.lua:220 (twice), Observer.lua:52, Map.lua:261; written as literals at Observer.lua:54 and Sync.lua:187; restated in the Core.lua:77 comment.
items.why: Persisted in SavedVariables (anchors), so the literals must stay, but nothing names the set once: a typo such as `"You"` at any read site type-checks and silently makes every sighting look like another player's (losing OWN_TRUST and the 'by you' tooltip). A `---@alias SPFSightingSource "you"|"player"` on both fields (or named constants) lets LuaLS catch it. Listed in the project skill Anti-patterns.
items.reason: Sync.lua assigns source locally after decoding, and Core.lua propagates it into both string-typed fields without conversion; an in-memory comparison typo bypassed OWN_TRUST. An optional literal-union annotation preserves existing saved values and nil handling, so the persistence exception does not excuse the untyped internal set.

items.quote: local agree = route.kind == "lift" and 2000 or AGREE
items.what: Per-route fit tuning lives in two homes: the generated `route.fit` table (samples, span, speed; tools/gen_transit.py:164, Data/Transports.lua) and hard-coded `route.kind == "lift"` overrides in Model.lua:89 (near radius 10) and Model.lua:123 (agree window 2000). Canonical home: `route.fit`, which Model.FitEpoch and Observer already read.
items.why: Both copies encode the same fact (lifts, especially UC's 3.5 s ride, need tighter fitting; the generator comment and Model's comment both cite it). Retuning one lift, or adding a kind that needs the narrow window (e.g. a tram car), means editing the generator and Model separately; Model's override also applies to every lift while the generator already distinguishes UC from TB/Great Lift. Accidental drift, not a stated hot-path specialisation.
items.reason: gen_transit.py sets per-route minimum sample count, observation span and speed; Model.lua sets spatial proximity and epoch-offset clustering tolerances, which are separate contracts with no duplicated parameter. The model spec passed, and in-memory probes demonstrated that sample/span thresholds change acceptance independently of proximity and clustering, supporting the lens's coincidental-similarity exclusion.

items.quote: return ok and type(value) == "table" and value or {}
items.what: Table() turns a non-string source, a loadstring failure, a runtime error or a non-table result from QuestieDB's ZoneDB private maps into {} with no signal.
items.why: Build (:61) checks only that zones.private exists, then (:68-71) decodes areaIdToUiMapId etc. through Table(). If QuestieDB changes that private shape (e.g. ships a table rather than a string, which the type(source) == "string" test rejects), every spawn's map resolves to nil (:110), index stays empty, state still becomes "ready" (:162), and the panel reports every service 'unavailable here'. The boundary is another addon's private field, so the guard is justified, but the failure is silent; setting state = "unavailable" (or geterrorhandler) when the area table decodes empty would surface it.

items.why: The code keeps the tree on the cached entry until it drops out of the eight-entry endTrees list or Grid.Idle clears it. Suggested wording: 'Keep their small entrance-cost vectors, and only the last eight grid trees; cap the cache ...'

items.quote: else -- neighbouring entrances across a cluster border
items.what: When two consecutive hops share a cluster (ka == kb) but the refining grid search fails, the else branch still runs and adds just the two entrance nodes, so the walk is drawn as a straight segment between them with no reason surfaced; the comment also only describes the cross-border case
items.why: The abstract A* already accepted the hop and returned its cost, so the callback receives a normal points/cost result whose drawn segment may cross walls, not a Path failure reason. Reaching it needs a baked intra-cluster edge that the decoded grid cannot walk (baker/runtime mismatch), which is rare; either split the branches so the ka == kb failure is surfaced (or at least logged in the debug trace), or state in the comment that the straight fallback is intended
items.reason: gen_nav.py:grid_hpa creates intra-cluster edges only between reachable nodes, and runtime searches verified all 720,486 shipped directed intra-cluster edges across all three maps are reachable. The alleged failure requires a separate, unestablished violation of that generated-data invariant.
